2.21    P21: Approximation of ﬁber-selected sections by a base singularity
Status: open in the stated generality. Book locator: Problem 32.9.2, printed p. 897.
Setup and scope. The complete statement below ﬁxes every geometric datum. The descent
H 0 (X, π ∗ Am ) = H 0 (B, Am ) uses compact connected ﬁbers. Its selected subspaces can nevertheless
record singularities upstairs that are not pullbacks of any one base potential.
Full problem statement. Let π : X → B be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected
compact complex manifolds with connected ﬁbers, where B is Kähler of dimension q ≥ 1. Fix a
Hermitian form ω on X, a holomorphic line bundle A with a smooth Hermitian metric h on B, and
φ ∈ PSH(X, ω). Set θ = c1 (A, h). For positive integers m, identify
                                    (                   )
                          Vm = H 0 X, π ∗ Am ⊗ I(mφ) ⊆ H 0 (B, Am )

by holomorphic descent. Find geometric or analytic conditions that produce ψ ∈ PSH(B, θ) of
positive non-pluripolar mass such that, for all suﬃciently large m,
                                          (                 )
                               Wm = H 0 B, Am ⊗ I(mψ) ⊆ Vm ,
                                     dim Vm − dim Wm = o(mq ).

Determine which features of the singularities of φ along the ﬁbers suﬃce for this approximation.
State of the art. When the selecting data descend, the base equilibrium theorem gives a precise
limit. For isolated point constraints upstairs, ﬁberwise integrability yields base vanishing conditions;
the resulting codimension is lower order and kernel diﬀerences have vanishing normalized mass.
Horizontal projective regimes also have lower asymptotics stable under intermediate section spaces.
Remaining gap. Find ﬁberwise singularity or integrability hypotheses yielding one θ-psh ψ of
positive mass and the stated o(mq ) defect. A ﬁnite-codimension comparison is useful only after
constructing the base ideal series. The requested ψ must retain the positive-mass premise needed
for the base limit.
Sources.    Book, Proposition 26.8.1, Theorem 26.6.1; Chapter 26’s ﬁber and horizontal kernel
sections.

unchanged_original_task.problem:
Let $\pi:X\to B$ be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected compact complex manifolds with connected fibers, where $B$ is K\"ahler of dimension $q\geq1$. Fix a Hermitian form $\omega$ on $X$, a holomorphic line bundle $A$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $B$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(X,\omega)$. Set $\theta=c_1(A,h)$. For positive integers $m$, identify
\[
 V_m=H^0\bigl(X,\pi^*A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\varphi)\bigr)
          \subseteq H^0(B,A^m)
\]
by holomorphic descent. Find geometric or analytic conditions that produce $\psi\in\PSH(B,\theta)$ of positive non-pluripolar mass such that, for all sufficiently large $m$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 W_m=H^0\bigl(B,A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\psi)\bigr)\subseteq V_m,\\
 \dim V_m-\dim W_m=o(m^q).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Determine which features of the singularities of $\varphi$ along the fibers suffice for this approximation.

Conventions: dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial; PSH(Y,alpha) consists of upper-semicontinuous quasi-psh u with alpha+dd^c u>=0. I(tu) consists of holomorphic germs g for which |g|^2 exp(-tu) is locally integrable. The non-pluripolar top mass means the total mass of the non-pluripolar product of the indicated positive current.
unchanged_original_task.completionCriteria: Answer every requested clause with complete proofs under explicitly stated geometric or analytic sufficient conditions. The statement asks for conditions, and does not assert that arbitrary upstairs selecting weights admit a base reference. Supply a nonempty family of admissible non-descended selectors, prove the base potential is theta-psh with finite positive non-pluripolar mass, prove the inclusion for all sufficiently large m and an o(m^q) dimension defect, and explain exactly which fiber singularity features ensure it. Retain the stated compactness, connected-fiber, Kahler-base and norm-independent space conventions. Check integer endpoints and dimension q=1. Distinguish any new anisotropic result from the previously proved isotropic section-over-divisor result, and do not claim a necessary-and-sufficient classification beyond what is proved.

applications.judgment: The primary operator is i/pi times partial barpartial. Its log inverse norm formula yields exactly the task i/(2pi) squared-norm formula; D is a reduced divisor of a nonzero defining section. Demailly agbook equation13.2 independently corroborates normalization.

Lemma2.1 is for an exact smooth real(1,1) form on a compact Kahler manifold. u=2pi times its potential converts normalization. This proves the residual Kahler-class equivalence in the accepted note; the current paper assumes the actual positive residual and uses the smooth metric ratio for examples.

Section3.15 takes ample to mean a positive tensor power very ample and constructs the positive metric by pulling back Fubini-Study and taking its tensor root. This is the exact premise; its converse Kodaira assertion is unused. The primary self-reference to Example3.15 is a harmless typo for preceding Example3.14.

The defining truncation measure is local, discards the pole locus, and for small unbounded locus equals extension of the ordinary wedge off it when that mass is locally finite. Here off D the wedge is the smooth beta^q with finite mass, so the product is well-defined and equals beta^q, including q1 formula229. No arbitrary singular finite-mass assertion is imported.

Theorem5.24 requires closed pluripolar locus and local upper bounds. The product common zero locus is proper analytic and locally pluripolar; the quadratic correction of log Q is bounded above, so the upper-limit extension applies. The actual correction has limit minus-infinity at the locus. A decreasing regularization also reconstructs this particular application directly.

premise_three_scope_judgment: The three short BEGZ quotations do not alone prove the universally worded existence clause. The actual application has small unbounded locus D and finite smooth off-divisor mass beta^q; the complete root-read primary definition and finite-mass criterion prove existence and beta^q equality directly, including degree one. clause_assessment.proved: psi=u+c log norm(s_D)^2, theta+ddc psi=beta+c[D], product beta^q and mass integral beta^q>0.

clause_assessment.proved: I(m psi)=O(-floor(mc)D); global lower bound and Fubini prove W_m subset V_m for every m>=1.
V_m lies between vanishing orders L_m=floor(mc) and K_m=max(floor(mc-a),0). Their difference is at most ceil(a), and each restriction layer is O(m^(q-1)).
Small logarithms of anisotropic squared section norms on B times (P1)^f meet a proper subset of each relevant fiber; positive metrics and a finite-chart curvature bound give admissibility.
